description: pip_requirements is DELIBERATELY absent, and the reason is narrower and sharper than
'it would manage the renderings'. Renovate's pattern for that manager is
(^|/)[\w-]*requirements([-._]\w+)?\.(txt|pip)$, which allows AT MOST ONE [-._]\w+
group after 'requirements' -- and \w excludes '-'. Measured 2026-08-23 against all
five renderings: only requirements-ci.txt matches. The four narrow slices
(requirements-ci-test.txt, -ci-audit.txt, -ci-mutation.txt, requirements-runtime-ci.txt)
are two-segment names and cannot match.
That is LUCK, not design, and it is the reason this note exists: renaming any narrow
slice to a single-segment name -- requirements-test.txt, say -- would silently bring it
into pip_requirements' scope. And the one file that DOES match is the 80-pin full
rendering, the most widely consumed of the five.
All five are GENERATED from uv.lock by scripts/sync-requirements-ci.sh. Renovate would
raise PRs bumping pins inside generated files, each failing check-requirements-ci, and
any that landed would be reverted by the next `make sync-requirements-ci`. The
declaration is pyproject.toml; the renderings are output. pep621 is the manager that
belongs and pip_requirements is the one that looks like it does.
pinDigests implements ADR-0006, which mandates SHA-pinning all GitHub Actions refs and
adding this key. Measured: this repo is 0 of 6 refs pinned, all actions/checkout@v6.
pinDigests makes Renovate pin currently-unpinned refs rather than only preventing new
drift, so it converges the gap instead of freezing it.
npm manages one dependency, json2yaml, which no lib/, scripts/ or Makefile line
invokes -- see the backlog row. Enabled rather than skipped so the dead dependency
becomes visible as a PR instead of rotting silently.
